messages:
pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT PAGER: kvcache_hosted_prod OOM spikes on runtime pool 'hosted-std-8' — severity: high :rotating_light:

alice: acked. I'm oncall for runtime, jumping in. seeing increased OOMs across 3/8 machines.

devon: getting the alerts too. metrics show kvcache_total_bytes per-pod went from ~1.7GB to ~13GB in ~15m. possible runaway prefetch?

sre-oncall: @alice @devon assign: emergency mitigation (throttle prefetch + reduce batch window) + collect flame graphs. Can someone check recent deploys?

alice: rolling deploy history looks clean, but we did push a prefetch tuning change yesterday to aggressive prefetch on long-contexts: `PREFETCH_TRIGGER_TOKENS=2048 -> 512`.

kevin: that aligns. new config increases aggressive prefetch for longer sequences. probably combining with continuous batching causes large KV materialization per request.

emily-cs: we have one customer report of long-form summarization timeouts ~10:02 UTC, they saw partial outputs then error. CS will triage affected orgs and flag any SLAs.

devon: logs from node hosted-std-8-03: `kvcache_alloc: request_id=xyz oom allocating 4.2G KV window` then `runtime: sigsegv/oom`. attaching tail snippet:

```
2026-03-15T10:11:06Z runtime.ERROR kvcache: alloc failed: wanted=4398046511104 bytes
2026-03-15T10:11:06Z runtime.ERROR serve: request=abc123 status=500 reason=oom
2026-03-15T10:11:08Z monitor.INFO node-health: restarting container
```

alice: immediate mitigation plan: 1) revert PREFETCH_TRIGGER back to 2048 on hosted runtime config; 2) lower continuous batching max_window to 256 tokens temporarily; 3) cordon and force-restart the 3 worst nodes to reclaim memory. Any objections?

kevin: +1. we should also throttle incoming long-context requests via gateway by returning 413 for > 32k tokens until we stabilize. I'll open a gateway rule.

sre-oncall: do it. Alice, take the revert. Devon, patch batching config and open the rollout with canary 10% -> 50% -> 100%. We want fast but not all-at-once.

alice: reverting PREFETCH_TRIGGER now. `kubectl set env deploy/hosted-runtime PREFETCH_TRIGGER_TOKENS=2048 --namespace=hosted` rolling update started.

kevin: gateway tunable pushed: `max_tokens_per_request=32768`, `reject_long_inputs=true` (immediate). Adding header X-Preview-Throttled for diagnostics.

devon: batching patch submitted: `continuous_batch.max_window=256` and `batching.enabled=true` rollout initiated. Canary on 2 pods first.

pagerduty-bot: update: 3 incidents acknowledged.

alice: cordoning node hosted-std-8-03 and restarting containers. watching pod memory.

(T+8m) devon: after revert + batching change: per-pod kvcache peaks reduced to ~2.1GB. OOMs stopped. node restarts completed.

emily-cs: CS update: affected customer (acct: acme-analytics) reported degraded experience for ~12 minutes, no data loss. we've opened a case and offered 10% credit.

kevin: we've also flagged model-serving logs for regressions to evaluate whether certain prompt patterns trigger prefetch in spite of trigger threshold.

alice: immediate post-incident notes: root cause likely interaction between overly-aggressive prefetch threshold + continuous batching that merged many long requests into one big KV window. Prefetch change lowered token threshold but didn't account for bursty batching.

devon: follow-ups (assigned):
- revert is in prod and stable (alice)
- permanent fix: add safety caps in kvcache allocator to refuse single-KV > 4GB and surface metric `kvcache.window_size.max` (devon)
- gating: add integration tests that simulate batching + prefetch (kevin)
- observability: add alert if kvcache_total_bytes growth rate > 1GB/min (sre-oncall)
- customer comms: CS to compile impacted org list and notify (emily-cs)

sre-oncall: I'll schedule a handoff to next-day oncall and create an incident ticket in JIRA with sev=high. Include the timeline and the `kubectl` commands used.

alice: commands used for rollback/mitigation (for ticket):
```
kubectl set env deploy/hosted-runtime PREFETCH_TRIGGER_TOKENS=2048 -n hosted
kubectl apply -f batching-patch.yaml -n hosted
kubectl cordon hosted-std-8-03
kubectl delete pod -l node=hosted-std-8-03 -n hosted
```

kevin: adding temporary runtime guard in gateway as a short-term safety net. We'll monitor token distribution and batching deltas.

emily-cs: noted for customer update. I'll send an initial msg to affected customers stating root cause suspected and mitigation steps taken.

devon: logging follow-up: add sampling of long-prompt traces (without customer PII) to help reproduce. Also add a metric for prefetch_trigger_count to correlate.

sre-oncall: handoff: assigning follow-ups to owners, pinging @oncall-tomorrow. Next steps: postmortem doc due EOD tomorrow, include timeline + action owners + ETA for permanent guard.

alice: thanks everyone. I'll keep monitoring for 1h and then close the incident thread if stable. :white_check_mark:
